title: Private Tier Upgrade Playbook + Terraform Ops & Customer Notices
content:
Purpose
This playbook bundles customer-facing maintenance/upgrade notification templates plus an operator-focused checklist for performing upgrades to Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It is intended for use by the private-deployments on-call and release teams when planning planned maintenance, minor/major upgrades, or emergency hotfixes that may affect customer SLAs/SLOs.

Scope and audience
- Scope: private VPC and on-prem installations managed by Redwood (control plane-assisted upgrades) and customer-managed on-prem installs where Redwood provides step-by-step guidance.
- Audience: release engineering, solutions engineering, customer success (CS), support, and SREs who execute or coordinate upgrades and customer communications.

High-level SLO impact summary (how to decide notice level)
- Non-disruptive config updates (no restart): SLO impact: none. Internal note: still send FYI notice for records.
- Rolling patch (node restart but rolling, <5% of capacity down per stage): Possible transient latency spike; SLO impact: soft (notifications recommended).
- Controlled mini-downtime (canary + brief fallbacks, expected <5 minutes per shard): SLO impact: low; send formal notice.
- Full cluster restart or DB migration with read-only window: SLO impact: medium/high; send multiple formal notices, schedule maintenance window, provide rollback plan.
- Emergency unplanned work: treat as incident communications.

Communication ownership and cadence
- Release lead (R-L): owner of the upgrade, responsible for sending the initial notice, coordinating CS and support messaging.
- CS lead: ensures customer account owners are informed and helps schedule timing for high-impact customers.
- SRE on-call: responsible for live monitoring during the window and post-check verification.
- Communications cadence: initial announcement (72–48 hours), reminder (24 hours), final reminder (2 hours), start notice, completion notice + post-maintenance report within 4 business hours.

Templates: customer-facing notices (editable)
Note: replace ALL-CAPS markers before sending.
1) Initial announcement (72–48 hours)
Subject: Planned maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment (ALL-CUSTOMER-NAME) – DATE/TIME
Body: Hello ALL-CUSTOMER-NAME team,

We are planning a planned upgrade to your Redwood Private deployment on DATE (WINDOW START – WINDOW END, TIMEZONE). The work will include: short bullet list (e.g., runtime security patch, kernel update, minor DB schema migration). Expected customer impact: STATE expected (none / brief rolling restarts / read-only window). Estimated duration: ESTIMATED_DURATION.

Why: brief justification (bugfix/security/perf).
What we will do to minimize disruption: rolling upgrades, canary first, traffic routing to healthy nodes, backups before any migration.
Actions requested from you: please ensure critical workloads are paused or scheduled outside the window if you expect heavy batch jobs; share any blackout dates.
Support: CS contact NAME (email) & Support channel link.
Regards,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

2) 24-hour reminder
Subject: Reminder: maintenance for Redwood Private deployment – DATE/TIME
Body: Short summary of changes and clear expected impact. Call out maintenance owner and a link to status page and support slack. Include a one-line rollback contingency statement.

3) 2-hour / 30-minute pre-start alerts
Subject: Starting maintenance for Redwood Private deployment in 2 hours
Body: Immediate brief: start time, expected duration, phone bridge/Zoom link for live ops, and how to reach emergency support.

4) Start notice (minutes)
Subject: Redwood maintenance window STARTING now – (ALL-CUSTOMER-NAME)
Body: We have started the maintenance window. We will post progress updates as bullets (canary started, canary healthy, rolling batch 1, etc.).

5) Completion notice & post-maintenance summary
Subject: Maintenance completed for Redwood Private deployment – DATE
Body: Completed at TIME. Summary of actions taken (version numbers, terraform plan/apply summary), verification checks passed, customer-facing impact (none/brief), open follow-ups (list), rollback performed? (yes/no), links to detailed change log and optional telemetry summary.

6) Post-maintenance health report (within 4 hours)
- SLO metrics snapshot (latency, error rate, throughput) comparing 2 hours pre-window vs 2 hours post-window.
- Any regressions and remediation steps.

Operator runbook: pre-maintenance checklist
- Confirm maintenance window and customer approval (timestamped).
- Prepare repo: branch off release branch, update module versions, verify PR linked to JIRA.
- Terraform: run terraform plan in a dedicated workspace. Save plan output artifact and attach to PR.
- State lock: ensure the state backend (S3/GCS/Consul) is reachable and locking works. Test lock acquisition on a staging workspace.
- Backups: snapshot critical state (DB snapshot, object store snapshot, etc.) and ensure backup retention policy applies.
- DB migrations: if present, prepare migration runbook and test in staging with identical data size where feasible; prepare read-only window steps.
- Canary baseline: choose a small batch of nodes to upgrade first and run smoke tests.
- Monitoring: ensure dashboards and alert rules are primed (pager escalations correct) and that log aggregation and trace sampling are active.
- Communication: prewrite notices and confirm CS distribution list.

Terraform-specific operational notes
- Backends: prefer remote state backends with object locking (S3 + DynamoDB / GCS with locking). Do not run concurrent terraform applies.
- Workspaces: use explicit workspace per customer-deployment (workspace naming: customerid-env). Avoid sharing state between customers.
- Module versioning: pin module versions in each customer overlay; use module semver tags and avoid floating 'latest'.
- Drift detection: run terraform plan --refresh and compare to last-known-good before apply. If plan shows large unexpected changes, pause and escalate.
- Sensitive changes: any change touching network resources (VPC, subnets, route tables) requires a second engineer review and CS approval.
- Rollback patterns: prefer terraform rollback by applying the previous commit (git tagged state) and running terraform apply with the previous plan, not manual resource deletions.

Example terraform commands (ops)
- terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=...
- terraform workspace select customer-123-prod || terraform workspace new customer-123-prod
- terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=upgrade.plan
- terraform apply "upgrade.plan"

If CRS (control plane-assisted upgrade) is in use:
- Ensure control-plane agent is at compatible version with the targeted runtime. Confirm agent heartbeat is green. Pause automated rollouts in the control plane UI and run manual canary first.

Rollout and verification plan
- Stage 0: Pre-checks (schema validation, backup exists).
- Stage 1: Canary on 1–2 nodes; run smoke tests and perf probes for 15–30 minutes.
- Stage 2: Rolling batches (10–25% of nodes per batch) with health checks between batches.
- Stage 3: Validation after final batch (system-wide tests, SLO smoke tests).
- Stage 4: Optional capacity increase / scale test to verify throughput.

Rollback procedure (if validation fails)
- Immediate: stop the upgrade pipeline and pause further applies. Re-route traffic to healthy pools if available.
- If limited batch failure: terminate affected nodes and spin up previous version nodes (via terraform apply previous plan or control-plane rollback).
- If DB migration failed: restore DB snapshot and perform a coordinated rollback; inform customer and trigger incident response.
- Post-rollback verification: check SLOs, run smoke tests, collect logs and timeline, and file a postmortem if impact >SLO threshold.

Customer segmentation notes (who to treat specially)
- High-SLA customers: require 72-hour notice and a pre-scheduled dry-run with their engineering contact.
- Regulated industries: assume on-prem packages; require signed maintenance window approvals and stricter rollback SLAs.
- Multi-tenant VPC customers: coordinate with infra team for network-level changes 2+ weeks in advance.

Escalation contacts (internal)
- Release lead: Priya Shah (pager/email)
- SRE lead: Ethan Martinez
- Solutions eng escalation: Lena Hoffmann
- CS escalation: Carlos Rivera
Include phone/pg links in the internal metadata (on call roster).

Post-deployment checklist and artifacts to attach
- terraform plan output, apply log, and the git commit/PR that triggered the upgrade.
- Monitoring snapshots (pre/post SLO graphs).
- Customer-facing completion email copy and a link to a support ticket with timeline.
- Any follow-up Jira tasks.

Appendix: quick editable copy snippets (short)
- "Planned upgrade (non-disruptive): expected no downtime; we will monitor for 2 hours and follow up with a short report."
- "Planned upgrade (rolling restarts): we expect transient latency increases up to X% for short bursts; production traffic will be routed to healthy nodes."

Notes and open questions (internal)
- Consider adding a per-customer maintenance preference flag in our control plane: preferred maintenance windows, notification channel, and preferred approver.
- Investigate automated pre-checks that can generate the terraform plan diff and highlight risky changes (network, DB schema, state locks).
- Align with legal on language for scheduled maintenance and SLA credits statement for customers with private deployments.

End of document
